topStory.text: NVIDIA's 8-K discloses residual value guaranties backstopping OpenAI's leases at SB Energy's PORTS Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio — roughly 4.25 GW of IT load, with NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation cumulatively capped at $105B and discretion to add credit support for about 3.8 GW more. If OpenAI defaults or becomes insolvent, NVIDIA pays the shortfall between each lease's guaranteed minimum value and what a replacement lease or sale recovers; the obligation lapses once OpenAI achieves a satisfactory credit rating, and OpenAI has agreed to reimburse NVIDIA for any amount it actually pays. Leases are expected to reach ready-for-service beginning in 2028. The chip supplier is now underwriting its largest customer's real estate.

feed.text: Bloomberg's analysis of BloombergNEF data counts 99 proposed on-site natural-gas plants — about 126 GW across 22 states, more than a third of it in Texas — being built to power US data centers. Run at industry-standard rates they would emit roughly 318 million metric tons of CO2 a year, lifting US power-sector emissions about 20%, and up to a third if run flat out. Amazon's Pecos County, Texas site and Microsoft's West Texas complex behind a Chevron-built plant account for more than 10 GW and up to 45 Mt CO2e between them.

The 60-day deadline arrived for all six FERC-jurisdictional RTOs/ISOs — PJM, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE and CAISO — to answer FERC's June 18 show-cause orders, which preliminarily found their large-load interconnection rules may be 'unjust, unreasonable or unduly discriminatory.' Each had to justify its existing tariff or propose reforms for connecting loads of 50 MW or more at 69 kV and above. Interested parties now get 30 days to respond to those filings, closing the comment window around Sep 16.

PJM formally filed its large-load framework at FERC in docket ER26-3515, requesting an Oct 12, 2026 effective date. Any site adding 50 MW or more of cumulative peak demand after June 1, 2027 must designate qualifying new capacity at least equal to its peak, and any unsupported portion is curtailed ahead of pre-emergency demand response — exposure a load can reduce or eliminate through the 'bring your own new capacity' (BYONC) path. PJM's case for it: roughly 70 GW of new large load projected by 2038 against about 15 GW of generation retired since 2022.

feed.text: Rep. Andrea Salinas (D-Ore.) introduced the Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026 (H.R. 10102), which would levy a federal excise tax of 1 cent per kilowatt-hour on electricity used by data centers above 1 MW of maximum rated capacity or peak load, raising an estimated $1.76B a year split evenly across the Land and Water Conservation Fund, Housing Trust Fund, Superfund, Highway Trust Fund and a new energy-technology fund. It was referred to Ways and Means with no clear path to passage; critics note a flat consumption tax does not distinguish between loads by their actual grid impact.

More than two-thirds of the electricity sought for US AI data centers is unlikely to ever materialize, per new Wood Mackenzie projections: grid operators and utilities will likely commit to only about 28% of the 1,066 GW currently requested nationwide, with the rest 'phantom' — duplicative or non-binding requests filed at multiple utilities simultaneously with no realistic path to construction.

NVIDIA signed MOUs with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish financing platforms mobilizing more than $500B of third-party capital for AI infrastructure — structured so outside investors fund data centers and power for NVIDIA's own customers (frontier labs, enterprises, AI clouds) without loading its balance sheet, with NVIDIA compute itself treated as the investable collateral. Subject to final agreements.

HD Hyundai Heavy Industries secured a $675M deal — its largest-ever power-engine order — to supply 1,000 MW of HiMSEN gas-engine generating capacity to a US data center project via developer Coban Energy Group, underscoring how quickly demand for on-site/behind-the-meter generation equipment is scaling.

NVIDIA will reportedly invest $2B for roughly 20% of Lancium — the Blackstone-backed Texas developer whose Abilene campus is Stargate's first operational site — at about a $10B valuation, extendable to $3B on milestones including grid hookups. Reported, not confirmed by the companies.

Amazon is backing what could be the largest natural-gas power plant ever built in the US — up to 7.6 GW of behind-the-meter generation planned for a data center site in Pecos County, Texas — and confirmed talks to develop a data center at the 4.5 GW gas plant under construction at Homer City, PA, as developers have proposed roughly 90 GW of behind-the-meter gas nationwide since the start of 2025 per Cleanview.

Oncor CEO Allen Nye told investors the utility's large-load service requests climbed to 298 GW from 289 GW at the end of Q1, with roughly 44 GW of projects in its territory qualified for ERCOT's Batch Zero interconnection review — a queue whose timeline is now unclear after Gov. Abbott's audit order, though Oncor said it supports the state's screening effort.

AWS is reportedly telling its own engineers to cut CPU waste and reclaim low-utilization EC2 instances to preserve capacity for customers — a sign the AI-era compute crunch is tight enough that the largest cloud is rationing internally, echoing capacity-constraint talk across hyperscaler Q2 calls.

BloombergNEF put numbers on the Texas freeze: the pause touches about 49.8 GW of projects — roughly 20% of the entire US data center pipeline — and could put up to $8 billion of data center revenue at risk by Q1 2027, with more than 70% of the ~50 GW BNEF tracks in Texas still at an early stage.

Bloomberg reports that rapid, synchronized power swings from AI training workloads are physically damaging data center equipment — batteries, generators and cooling systems are malfunctioning or wearing out well ahead of schedule — adding unplanned costs and reliability risk for operators even as rack densities climb toward 100 kW.

PJM's board sent FERC its full large-load framework — an Interim Resource Adequacy Service creating a registry of every 50+ MW load and a 'bring your own new capacity' (BYONC) path for data centers to contract new generation, storage or demand response — under which, starting June 2027, large loads that don't bring capacity are curtailed ahead of pre-emergency load management, with states and utilities deciding who gets cut.

NRG said on its Q2 call it has aligned on principal commercial terms with an unnamed global cloud and AI hyperscaler for a $3.2 billion, 1.2 GW combined-cycle gas plant in Texas — a 15-year minimum contract with an investment-grade counterparty targeting late-2029 commercial operation and expandable to 2.4 GW, with 95% of free cash flow underpinned by capacity payments regardless of data center utilization.

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott directed the PUCT and ERCOT to audit all 1,800+ projects in the state's 474 GW large-load interconnection queue (~90% data centers) and paused approvals of new data center connections until each project's power demand, water use, public financial assistance and ownership are verified — prompting ERCOT to postpone its Batch Zero transmission planning study.
